rubrics.rubric: Does the revised rehearsal schedule cover Sep 15-27, resolve the Director's requested changes, and respect venue and personnel constraints?
criterion: The Daily Schedule has one row for each rehearsal day in the Sep 15-27 period.
Each rehearsal row reports date, day, venue or room, start time, end time, meal break when applicable, rehearsal hours, activity, and cast called.
Weekly rehearsal-hour subtotals are shown for Sep 15-21 and Sep 22-28.
Days off are listed.
The added Sep 17 rehearsal uses rooms and times that are actually available.
The Sep 20 full-company stumble-through resolves the Main Hall conflict using a feasible venue plan.
The Conflict Matrix cross-references cast availability against rehearsal dates.
Maria Santos is treated as available after Sep 11.
Priya Mehta's Tuesday arrival constraint is reflected in her calls and activity sequencing.
Production-team constraints that affect the scheduled activity, including piano and choreography availability, are respected.

rubrics.rubric: Does the schedule demonstrate compliance with the applicable Theatre UCF rehearsal rules?
criterion: Each Monday-Sunday week remains within the 23-hour pre-technical-rehearsal maximum.
Weeknight rehearsals last no more than four hours.
Weeknight rehearsals begin no earlier than 6:00 PM and end no later than 10:30 PM.
Ordinary weekend calls schedule no more than seven work hours in an eight-hour span.
Ordinary weekend calls include a one-hour meal break after no more than five work hours.
Any use of the handbook's straight-six option documents that all stated prerequisites are satisfied.
Each weekend preserves one complete 24-hour day without rehearsal.
The workbook includes a rule-by-rule compliance check using the cited handbook.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Reconciliation sheet tie every budget category to the underlying expense records?
criterion: Every Budget Summary category appears, including categories with zero actual spending.
Each row reports Budgeted, Actual Spent from the Budget Summary, Sum of Expense Details, Receipt numbers, Match, Uncommitted Balance, and Variance Flag.
Expense-detail sums include every receipt mapped to the category.
The Match field reflects whether the summary actual equals the expense-detail sum.
Uncommitted balance equals budgeted amount minus the reconciled actual amount.
Any category-name normalization between the two source sheets is disclosed.
Reconciliation totals tie to the source budget total and source actual-spent total.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Cash Flow Forecast provide a coherent weekly projection from Sep 15 through Oct 19?
criterion: The forecast has one row per Monday-Sunday week from Sep 15 through Oct 19.
The opening position uses actual spending and actual revenue received to date from the budget tracker.
Each week reports projected spending and projected revenue inflows.
Each week reports cumulative spending and cumulative revenue.
Each week reports the net cumulative position.
Every week with cumulative spending greater than cumulative revenue is flagged.
Revenue timing is consistent with the source notes, including the ticket-sales start date.
Material timing assumptions for uncommitted expenses are stated.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Reimbursement Action Items sheet include every expense requiring action and apply the priority rule correctly?
criterion: Every expense whose status is not paid, reimbursed, or direct payment appears in the action list.
Each action row reports receipt number, date, payee, amount, status, days outstanding, priority, and action.
Days Outstanding is calculated from September 15, 2025.
High priority is assigned when amount is greater than $200.
High priority is assigned when days outstanding is greater than 10.
An item exactly 10 days old and not over $200 is not classified High.
The total outstanding amount equals the sum of the listed nonzero action items.
Recommended actions identify a responsible next step.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Emergency Board Memo contain the required financial, scheduling, compliance, and decision content?
criterion: The memo is dated September 15, 2025 and identifies the Producer and Board.
The memo is approximately one to two pages.
The memo reports total budget, total spent, utilization percentage, and remaining balance from the reconciliation.
The memo reports actual and projected revenue and the resulting cash-flow gap.
The memo reports the total outstanding reimbursements.
The memo identifies upcoming major uncommitted expenses.
The memo explains the Sep 20 venue conflict and the selected resolution.
The memo reports material personnel-record compliance issues.
The memo reconciles script distribution records with the budget tracker's backorder note.
The memo makes a clear recommendation on the second-half budget tranche and supports it with displayed financial evidence.
The memo closes with an action table containing Priority, Item, Owner, Deadline, and Status.
The action table covers the material unresolved finance, venue, script, and personnel-compliance actions identified in the memo.

rubrics.rubric: Does the contact and compliance workbook provide a complete unified directory and actionable follow-up tracking?
criterion: Every cast member and production-team member appears once in a unified directory.
The directory contains all required contact, emergency-contact, script, compliance, action, owner, and deadline columns.
Cast emergency-contact data is carried over accurately.
Missing production-team emergency-contact data is identified as a follow-up item rather than invented.
Script status reflects the roster and the known backorder.
Personnel availability notes that affect scheduling are retained.
Compliance flags identify unresolved issues supported by the roster.
Each unresolved issue has a follow-up action, responsible party, and deadline.

rubrics.rubric: Are the four deliverables complete and mutually consistent?
criterion: The output contains one DOCX memo and three XLSX workbooks covering the four requested deliverables.
The schedule workbook contains Daily Schedule and Conflict Matrix sheets.
The budget workbook contains Reconciliation, Cash Flow Forecast, and Reimbursement Action Items sheets.
Names, dates, financial totals, conflicts, and action owners are consistent across the deliverables.
